entities.summary: Pantaleon, a 4th-century Christian martyr and healer, played a significant role in the Diocletianic Persecution of 305 AD in Nicomedia, Bithynia. Born into a devout Christian family, Pantaleon's faith was tested during the reign of Emperor Diocletian, who sought to eradicate Christianity. Despite facing brutal persecution, Pantaleon continued to heal the sick and serve the poor, earning him the respect and admiration of his community. His martyrdom on July 28, 305 AD, solidified his status as a holy figure in both Western and Eastern Christianity. Pantaleon's legacy extends beyond his own time, inspiring countless saints, martyrs, and healers throughout history. As one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers of the Late Middle Ages, Pantaleon's name became synonymous with devotion, healing, and selfless service. His example continues to guide Christians around the world, reminding us of the transformative power of faith and compassion.
